findings.evidence: **Unique keys accept many NULLs** in PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite. If a missing value must also be unique, use PostgreSQL 15+ `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT` or make the column `NOT NULL`.
findings.fix: Shorten this to the non-obvious part: 'For a nullable column that must also be unique when missing, use PostgreSQL 15+ `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT`.' The model already knows that NULLs do not collide in unique keys. Apply the same trim to the MyISAM line (line 40), keeping only the 'no warning' fact.

findings.evidence: Use one nullable FK per parent type plus `CHECK (num_nonnulls(article_id, photo_id) = 1)` on PostgreSQL, or a shared supertype table the FK can target.
findings.fix: Choose a default and give the condition for the alternative: 'Default: one nullable FK per parent type plus `CHECK (num_nonnulls(...) = 1)`. Switch to a shared supertype table only when there are more than about three parent types, or when new parent types are added often.'
